newsitem.title: USA: CALIF. LEGISLATURE OKS $7 BLN UTILITY BOND BILL.
newsitem.headline: CALIF. LEGISLATURE OKS $7 BLN UTILITY BOND BILL.

text.p: California's Senate gave final approval on Thursday to a bill making it easier for the state to issue a record $7 billion of bonds to help investor-owned utilities compete in a deregulated market.

The state Senate approved the bill on a vote of 27-to-2 with little debate. The Assembly approved the bill on Monday. Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, was expected to sign the measure into law in the coming weeks, a spokesman said.
"This is great for California," said Senator Steve Peace, who introduced the bill. "The ratepayers are protected. The workers are protected. It protects the environment."
"You're going to have (electricity) rates that are half of what they are today because of competition," Peace said.

The bonds are part of the state's effort to open its electricity industry to more competition. They will be issued by the state's infrastructure bank, but must be repaid by the investor-owned utilities benefiting from the bond sale.
Peace introduced the so-called "clean-up" bill earlier this year to make it easier for California to market the bonds. The state legislature approved the bond plan last year.
Peace's bill will ensure that the bonds retain their state tax-exempt status.
The bill will also allow the utilities to collect ratepayer charges beyond the current December 31, 2001 cutoff date, the senator's spokesman said.
The changes are expected to save state ratepayers an estimated $150 million by lowering bond borrowing costs, David Takashima, Peace's chief of staff, said.

Consumer advocates -- including Consumers Union and The Utility Reform Network -- had sought to derail Peace's bill, arguing that the bond plan would shift the cost of nuclear and other expensive utility investments back to consumers.
The state infrastructure bank is expected to come to market with $7 billion of the utility bonds in October.
The bill authorizes the state to sponsor up to $10 billion of bonds.

The bond proceeds will provide a revenue stream to investor-owned utilities, allowing them to reduce their rates and pay off debt on assets that will become less valuable as the industry is deregulated.
PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric and Edison International's Southern California Edison Co plan to issue the first tranche of bonds.
